# Check 3: residual diagnostics

## One-step-ahead residuals for compositions

Pearson residuals of multinomial compositions are correlated across bins (they must add up), so their patterns can
mislead. **One-step-ahead (OSA) residuals** (Trijoulet et al. 2023) condition each bin on the bins before it; under
a correct model they are independent N(0, 1). `ss3_resid()` computes them for the SS3 likelihood: multinomial with
the adjusted sample size, or Dirichlet-multinomial with the precision implied by the SS3 effective sample size.
Growth curves by sex (`lhpar`) track cohorts.

```{r res-osa, fig.height = 5}
rl <- ss3_resid(ss3simple)                   # length; ss3_resid(ss3simple, "age") for ages
ss3plot_resid(rl, lhpar = lh)
ss3plot_resid(rl, type = "qq")
```

Pacific hake uses the Dirichlet-multinomial for its age compositions:

```{r res-phk, fig.height = 4}
data(ss3phk)
ss3plot_resid(ss3_resid(ss3phk, "age"), cohorts = FALSE)
```

Conditional age-at-length data are a multinomial over ages for each length bin, so `ss3_resid(quant = "con")`
computes OSA residuals per length bin; `long = TRUE` keeps the bin for `ss3plot_caal()` (length bin by age, one
panel per year, with the growth curves). Runs tests, joint residuals and hindcasts use the mean age by length bin
combined over the bins (`quant = "con"`, as `ss3diags::SScompsTA1.8(type = "con")`), and generalised size
compositions are `quant = "size"`. None of the example models has conditional age-at-length data:

```{r res-caal, eval = FALSE}
d <- ss3_resid(ss3rep, quant = "con", long = TRUE)
ss3plot_caal(d, fleet = "Survey", lhpar = ss3_lhpar(ss3rep))
ss3plot_runs(ss3rep, quant = "con")
```

> **Reading OSA residuals.** Bins are conditioned on the smaller bins: too few small fish gives negative residuals
> at small sizes and positive residuals at larger sizes. Diagonal patterns that follow the growth curves are year
> classes the model does not fit.

## Runs tests and joint residuals

The runs test checks the log residuals of each index (or the mean length or age) for randomness; the 3-sigma
limits come from the average moving range (Carvalho et al. 2021). North Atlantic shortfin mako:

```{r res-runs, fig.height = 5}
data(ss3sma)
ss3_runs(ss3sma)
ss3plot_runs(ss3sma)
```

```{r res-jres, fig.height = 4}
ss3plot_jres(ss3sma)
```

> **Check 3: residuals.** Red flags: a failed runs test (p < 0.05), residuals outside the 3-sigma limits, trends
> in the joint residuals (lowess line), RMSE above 30%. Actions: look for conflicts between indices, changes in
> catchability, selectivity or growth; never drop data only to pass a test.
